text: The City of Do-nothings. There is no island " near Capreae," and "the neighbouring island of Capreae" is meaningless; if the text is sound, Suetonius is careless, or we must take Capreis as a locative, and regard vicinam as used in a partitive sense like reliquus, primus, etc. [1951 edition: The Land of Do-nothings. As there is no island "near Capreae," I take Capreis as locative, and vicinam as partitive. But see McDaniel, T.A.P.A., xlv. 17 ff. and Della Corte, Apragopoli, etc. and Augustiana (Naples, 1933, 1934). The latter reads Capreas and takes insula as "aggregato civico" (pagus or vicus).]
